findings.summary: On every empty cart, the vignette rule makes agents add a 'preview of the filled screen' next to the empty message: made-up line items with names, options, prices and a total, in tinted chips on a saturated blue panel. It reads as real cart data and contradicts the empty message. It also puts a second blue field right under the blue header band. The empty state's own art is a lone pair of overlapping discs. The reference gives an empty or feature panel one composed piece of art and never shows invented records.
findings.promptFix: Take 'an empty state as a 40%-opacity preview of the filled screen' out of the vignette's Where list. Add to the empty-state row: an empty state never shows sample records, names, prices or totals, whether real-looking or faded. It shows one shape-kit composition of the area's subject (or a size.glyphLg glyph), a title, one line and one ink pill, on a panel in the area hue, or on cream when a saturated field is already in view.
findings.specRule: Where. Hero and feature sections of front pages, onboarding and feature tours; an empty state as a 40%-opacity preview of the filled screen; a bubble holding the pop-dots glyph while an answer loads.

findings.summary: Header-band art is one small stamp, about 150px, that nearly every area repeats across all three apps: a crescent disc, a flat cloud and a pink sparkle, with the occasional hexagon-plus-pill. The disc-and-cloud version appears on the shop home, cart, checkout, projects, project detail, profile and security pages. The reference's bands carry a big, varied composition that fills roughly half the band: a blob-cut image with an offset edge, a cloud, a large four-point star, a bubble, all overlapping. Here the art is a small icon in an empty corner, so the bands read as a generic colored header with a sticker, not the reference's sunny scenes.
findings.promptFix: A header band's cluster spans 40–50% of the band's height (at least 200px tall on desktop) and is built from 3–5 shapes: one large lead shape, one medium overlapping shape, and sparkles in two sizes, one of them a large four-point star. Pick the lead shape for the area's subject (a sun, a moon, a blob, a hexagon, a pill or a cloud) and never let two areas of one product share a lead shape and layout. A disc with a small cloud beside it is one option among many, not the default.

findings.summary: On product detail pages, a saturated area-hue header band sits right above a large saturated item cover, often in the same yolk. Two big fields fill the desktop first screen and the whole phone screen, so the title and the product image blur together. The reference holds one field per view and puts white or cream between it and the next colored element.
findings.promptFix: One saturated field per viewport. When a detail page's item cover is wider than a third of the content, the header band turns cream (indigo at night) and the area hue appears only on its nav dot, tag and cluster, so the cover is the screen's one field. Two adjacent fields never share a hue, and white or cream of at least space.8 always separates two fields.

findings.summary: On phones, every header band drops its shape cluster onto a row of its own below left-aligned text. The band grows to 40–75% of the first screen, mostly empty color, and on product screens the header also takes two rows. On the blog home the vignette stacks the same way. The reference phone has one compact header row and a centered hero, with the art tucked against the band's edge or trimmed small. The spec says decoration 'moves last', and agents read that as moving it to a new row inside the band.
findings.promptFix: Below breakpoint.md, a compact header band is never taller than its text plus space.8 above and below plus the arc. Its cluster shrinks to 72–96px and sits absolutely in the band's top-right corner, behind nothing, with the text column kept clear of it. It never gets a row of its own and never reserves a column beside the text. Top nav stays one row: logo, the primary pill and a menu button, with links moved into the menu.

findings.summary: Text and top-bar nav links get a flush, square, sometimes lopsided focus box that touches the current-page dot. Sidebar and pill items show the reference's rounded ring 2px out, so it is the links that fall short. This was named in rc.1 and is still open. On the phone's scrolling section strip, the ring is clipped at the edge.

Confirmations are timid. A saved profile or a newsletter signup shows only a small inline tick and a word, often below the fold. The spec calls for an ink pill toast with a sparkle, which the add-to-cart state does well, and the reference states outcomes confidently. Data-table rows show no visible hover.

Small-scale art is thinner than the reference. Empty states carry a lone 40px blob, a zigzag or a pair of discs, sometimes in a grey-bordered white box. Settings plates and stat-tile plates fill about half their plate with little crescent shading. Option-row glyphs are arbitrary marks in one hue, unrelated to their labels. The reference fills its plates, picks each glyph for its label, and never borders a card.
Stat-tile figures are about 32px, and a white-plated, stock-looking icon in each tile competes with them. In the reference's color tiles a huge bold number dominates under a small eyebrow.

On the billing page, unselected plans are grey-outlined white (lilac-outlined indigo at night) boxes with small prices, a generic SaaS pricing grid. The reference uses borderless toned cards and big bold figures. This is still open from rc.1.

The front-page hero vignette is loose. The disc pins to one card's corner, and a lone sparkle and a stray dot float apart. The third card is an empty typing bubble that reads as a ghost strip. The reference's vignette overlaps product fragments, bubble, disc and sparkles into one tight scene.
Two phone layout slips by the agents. The footer email input collapses to a thin sliver. The scrolling section and tab strip leaves the active pill out of view, so nothing marks the current page.

notes: Review: 141/141 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/morning-shapes/0.1.0-rc.2/review-1).

All three apps clearly speak the reference's language: yolk, blue and green bands with sag arcs, ink pills on ledges, cream borderless cards, category-dot filter pills, saturated stat tiles and a convincing navy/indigo night palette. rc.1's scattered stickers and hue-swapped covers are fixed, and product covers now picture their subject well.

It still reads as a tidier, more generic cousin rather than the same team's work. Header-band art has shrunk to one repeated small disc-cloud-sparkle stamp in an empty corner, where the reference fills its bands with big, varied, overlapping scenes. Phone bands balloon with a stacked art row, detail pages stack two saturated fields, and the spec's empty-state 'preview' rule produces fake cart data. Fix the cluster scale and variety, the phone band, and the one-field rule to reach signature 4.
